brandReliability.rank_note: Below industry average. J.D. Power 2025 Vehicle Dependability Study ~243 PP100 vs industry avg 202 (higher = more problems, so worse than average). Consumer Reports has insufficient data for a full brand ranking.
brandReliability.predicted_owner_cost_note: High. Mercedes-Benz is generally the costliest of the German luxury brands to own long-term, driven by complex electronics, expensive parts/labour, and out-of-warranty repair bills.

warranty.notes: No separate longer powertrain term in Canada; basic and powertrain run together at 4 yr/80,000 km.

maintenance.complimentary_plan: None brand-wide. Star/Prepaid Maintenance is a paid add-on (pre-purchased scheduled service), not complimentary.
maintenance.notes: Mercedes is the costliest of the German luxury brands to maintain long-term. Estimates cover scheduled A/B services; brakes, tires, and wear items are extra. Synthetic oil, cabin filters, and brake fluid services add up quickly on AMG/V8/V12 models.
